title: An initial-state record guarantees 75 percent of onset-input information in symmetric passive circuit models
abstract: We tested temporal compression of a constant input that starts at recording onset in a symmetric passive stochastic circuit. The initial state was stationary for zero input and did not depend on input amplitude. A population time average alone had no positive uniform fraction of full-path Fisher information. Keeping the exact initial population state with that average gave a sharp lower bound of 75 percent. A score from the average and two endpoint projections retained all path information. We proved the bound and tested all 180 point inputs in twelve models from two partial adult worm electrical maps, with count and binary weights and three coupling scales. At one assumed leak time and primary count scale, median average-only fractions were 0.517 and 0.520. With initial-state recording they were 0.836 and 0.836. Independent covariance and transition checks agreed. These are model results. Exact observation, known symmetric dynamics, isotropic noise, incomplete anatomy and absent activity validation limit biological use. Original code, proof, aggregate evidence, a figure, hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External source records are excluded.

display.caption: Information fractions after input onset in two partial adult worm circuit models. Lines show point-input medians; bands show ranges. Exact initial-state recording gives the proved 75 percent bound under the stated model assumptions.
